fullPassage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that may not be part of its explicit definition. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.

④ mean ❌ 오류 — 주어가 'grasping the connotation of a word(단어의 함축의미를 파악하는 것)'라는 동명사구예요. 동명사구 주어는 하나의 덩어리라 단수로 취급하므로 동사도 단수형 means가 되어야 해요. mean은 복수형이라 틀림 ←정답

det.korean: a deeper insight=더 깊은 통찰
det.analysis:

③ a deeper insight(더 깊은 통찰) ✅ 정답 — 함축의미를 알면 대상 판단에 '더 깊은 통찰'을 얻음

④ no clear idea(분명한 개념이 없음) — 긍정적 결과와 정반대

det.analysis:

③ 일치 — 지시의미는 'basic, dictionary definition ... for any entity'라고 명시됨

④ 일치 — 함축의미는 'additional attributes and contexts'를 아우른다고 함

det.analysis:
'바로 이 특성들이 ~하는 것이다'는 'these are what(이것들이 바로 ~하는 것)'로 시작해요.
그다음 'make + 목적어(the word human) + 보어(applicable)' 구조로 'human을 적용 가능하게 만든다'를 만들어요. 보어 자리에는 형용사 applicable이 와요.
마지막에 '모든 개인에게'를 뜻하는 to all the individuals를 붙여요.
→ these are what make the word human applicable to all the individuals (12단어). the가 두 번(the word / the individuals) 쓰이는 점에 유의하세요.
det.tip: these are what + make+목적어+형용사(applicable) + to all the individuals

questions.wa: these are what make the word human applicable to all the individuals

questions.passage: In his exploration of how we engage with language, John Stuart Mill noted that there is a distinction between the denotation and connotation of words. The denotation of a word is its basic, dictionary definition —the straightforward umbrella term for any entity. For example, the term “human” denotes a person and can be used to refer to all human beings —Alice, Bill, and countless other individuals. To put it another way, denotation is the broad category of actual referents to which a word can be applied. Connotation, on the other hand, is more complicated as it encompasses all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that __________. The term “human,” according to Mill, embodies characteristics such as corporeality, biological life, the ability to reason, and a specific external form, and these are what make the word “human” applicable to all the individuals. In essence, grasping the connotation of a word means having a nuanced understanding of the entity the word refers to. By understanding the connotative meanings of a word, one gains a deeper insight into whether a particular object or individual falls within its denotative scope.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 조건에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
함축의미는 단어가 지니는 추가적 속성으로, 그 단어의 명시적 정의의 일부가 아닐 수도 있다.
...all the additional attributes and contexts a word can carry that __________.
[조건] (1) be, definition, explicit, its, may, not, of, part를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~아닐 수도 있다'는 조동사 may + not + be, '~의 일부'는 part of, '그것의 명시적 정의'는 its explicit definition으로 배열함
det.analysis:
'~아닐 수도 있다'는 '가능성'을 나타내는 조동사 may에 부정 not, 그리고 be동사를 이어 may not be로 만들어요.
'~의 일부'는 part of, '그것의 명시적 정의'는 소유격 its + 형용사 explicit + 명사 definition → its explicit definition.
→ may not be part of its explicit definition (8단어)
det.tip: may(~일 수도) + not + be + part of + its explicit definition
